summary:
## Idea
A compiled iterative pure tick reducer threads an immutable caller blackboard and saved state through memory/reactive composites, parallel thresholds and decorators. Explicit halt traces identify abandoned running leaf occurrences.

## Complexity
Work follows visited nodes and configured Repeat/Retry repetitions, with saved state proportional to program nodes. Reactive composites revisit higher-priority children. It is not unconditionally O(tree nodes) when repeat counts grow.

## Use when
Compose execution behaviours with deterministic resumption or priority interrupts.

## Avoid when
A planner must discover a sequence from goals, or a leaf cannot expose effects separately from its deterministic transition.

## Pitfalls
Sequence/Selector resume; reactive versions restart their guard scan. Halting invokes no callback: consume tickTracedWithHalts to cancel real effects. Occurrences, not leaf values, identify halts. Throwing leaves leave input state intact.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Decision.BehaviourTree.compile: BehaviourTree<'L> -> BtProgram<'L>`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Decision
let program = BehaviourTree.compile (BehaviourTree.Leaf "check")
let leaf _ board = BtStatus.Success, board + 1
let status, state, board =
    BehaviourTree.tick program leaf (BehaviourTree.initial program) 0
```

## Tests
BehaviourTreeTests: independent recursive interpreter, random-tree invariant/lifetime tracking, priority interrupt and halt ordering, repeated occurrences, tick atomicity, 100000-node stack-safety cases.

## Bench
The cited archived 0.2.0 baseline contains decision/behaviour-tree/ticks and decision/behaviour-tree/reactive-ticks. Read its source commit, host/date/toolchain, sizes, work counts, runtime-specific median/p95 and spread. These are GitHub-hosted runner-class comparisons, not quiet-host absolute performance; this later source revision is not itself remeasured.
